the Caulimoviridae family is a diverse group of plant viruses with a wide geographical distribution, that they are transmitted by mealybugs and that they are able to induce a range of symptoms in their natural hosts.
the Caulimoviridae family comprises two genera: Caulimovirus and Badnavirus.

understanding the role of the host in viral pathogenesis, the mechanisms involved in the regulation of gene expression, and the evolution of viral genomes.
understanding the molecular basis for the pathogenicity of plant pararetrovirus and the development of strategies for the control of pararetroviral diseases in plants.
the development of novel, non-toxic, anti-tumor agents.

the caulimovirus group is a distinct taxon, and that the badnavirus group is a separate taxon, which is closely related to, but not identical with, the caulimoviruses.

the caulimoviruses are a group of plant pararetroviruses that share a high degree of sequence homology and genome organization, and that are related to the badnaviruses, the only other group of plant pararetriviruses.
